messages.subject: CEO: Traversence vs Wix and Squarespace (costs vs benefits)
messages.body:
The 5-page PDF is in the CEO chat (download it there to review with Gemini). Bottom line:
1) Price. Core is $79.95/mo. Wix's commerce plans are $29–$159/mo billed yearly; Squarespace's are $19–$99/mo. Card processing is about the same everywhere (~2.9% + 30¢). Only Squarespace Basic adds a 2% platform fee. Core costs about $51/mo more than Wix Core or Squarespace Core at any sales volume.
2) Only we have: a place in the regional directory and guides (never paid ranking), GO Codes and short links, zero commission, manual payments on every plan, and local support.
3) They're stronger today: mature site builders and templates, app markets, abandoned-cart and email campaigns, bigger product limits (ours is 100 items on Core), and payments and domains that work now.
4) Our gaps before Core can sell e-commerce: card checkout and domains are built but not live (sandbox keys, domains in test mode); Core's 500 emails and campaigns aren't built; the site is still closed to search engines, so the local-traffic benefit can't be shown yet.
5) Suggestions in the PDF (not decided): turn on live payments and domains first; a first-year domain credit on yearly Core; revisit Core's item cap; measure each listing's referral traffic once the search lock lifts.
Competitor figures came from each company's own site through search results; confirm them on their pricing pages before deciding.

messages.subject: CEO: launch report, Nov 27
messages.body:
Today's launch report, against the six gates for Jan 1. Nothing is waiting for your OK.

GATES
1. Core paths: not yet. Most paths work on staging. Sign up and Like were faults in our checker, now being fixed. Typo search and set-my-place are fixed by releases already built.
2. 1A town paths: not yet. Eat, stay and see pass in all six towns. Two guides jump while loading (fix built). Winslow has no area yet (its fix, W15, is built). Test purchases can't reach Intuit's sandbox from our robots: one sandbox payment by a person will settle it, and it'll go with your own test.
3. Data: not yet. 1A's guides are at 55 to 62 against the 70 needed. Editorial is lifting them on public sources.
4. Safety: partly. The access hole is closed and the release pipeline is fixed (live). Our own nightly backups and the 7 days of on-time jobs are queued.
5. Money: not yet. The sandbox checklist hasn't passed, and your own $4.95 purchase and refund comes last. We found and are fixing a checkout fault (a business's copy of an order could be missed); no real money was affected, since cards are still on test keys.
6. Search: the lock holds; it lifts on your date.

WHAT MOVED TODAY
The pipeline fix is live. The goals plan, routing, budgets and silent sessions are recorded. The theater pilot is planned: the Hometown Theater sells the tickets, and restaurants join with in-person deals and GO Codes. Its event pages pass design review; the second is ready Nov 28, ahead of Dec 10 to 12.

NEXT, IN ORDER
R2, then the checkout fix, the goals catch-up and the goal check (Monday 6 AM), then the gate 1 and 2 fixes, the events build, backups, and your email links.

DECIDED BY THE TEAM TODAY (overturn any)
- Checkout's write into a business's records is recorded as a rule, granted only once its fix is live (CTO).
- A refund a business makes in its own Stripe or Square won't yet void our ticket. Fix: the business's own Mark refunded on the order, which voids its tickets, with a gateway link later (CFO). Queued under gate 5.
- From the 4th guest like of one thing on one shared connection in a day, the guest gets the free human check, then the like counts; never refused outright, as your 0009 note says. The limit stays 3 (CEO, for the theater night's shared wifi).

COMING TO YOU, NOT TODAY
Your one sandbox payment and the $4.95 test, with steps, once the checklist is ready. Live email before about Dec 14, so the theater's restaurant invites can go out. The search lock's date.

Spend today: $0 agent spend.
